concept.name: K-means clustering
concept.definition: A clustering algorithm that assigns observations to the nearest of k centroids and updates centroids to minimize within-cluster squared Euclidean distance.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Initialize k centroids, alternate nearest-centroid assignment and centroid recomputation, and stop when assignments or inertia stabilize.
concept.formula: Inertia = sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned centroid
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Six asset feature vectors are partitioned around two centroids, then centroids are recomputed from the assigned members.
